title: Order book heatmap
description: Bookmap-style liquidity heatmap: resting size by time and price drawn by the GPU, best bid and ask lines, trades as bubbles sized by volume, a profile of the current book, zoom, pan and a crosshair readout. Streams append one column per interval in a sliding window.

read.title: How to read it
read.text: The heatmap is a recording of the order book: every column is a snapshot of the book at one moment, laid out from left to right, with now at the right edge.
read.axes: The horizontal axis is time (newest on the right), the vertical axis is price. Hover anywhere: the crosshair reads the resting size at that price and time.
read.color: The color of a cell is the size resting at that price at that time: dark means almost nothing, brighter colors (blue → cyan → yellow → white) mean more. The legend at the top left gives the size range and unit of the colors.
read.walls: Bright horizontal lines are large orders that stay in the book (walls). Where a line ends, the order was pulled or filled: if the price line reaches the end of the wall, it was filled.
read.lines: The red and green lines that follow the price are the best ask and the best bid, the gap between them is the spread. On the price axis the filled red and green tags are the current best ask and bid, the outlined tag is the last trade.
read.bubbles: Dots are trades: green for aggressive buys (lifting asks), red for aggressive sells (hitting bids), their area grows with the volume traded during the column, so large bubbles are large trades. colorConvention="red-up" swaps the two colors.
read.profile: The bars on the right are the current book: asks in red above, bids in green below, longer bars mean more size; the scale below them is the size.

patterns.title: What to look for
patterns.hold: Support and resistance: the price touches a bright line several times and turns back, the large order absorbs it.
patterns.pull: Pulled orders (spoofing): a bright line disappears as the price comes close without any trade bubble there, the order was cancelled, not filled.
patterns.sweep: Sweeps: a burst of large bubbles crosses several prices, the price line jumps and the liquidity on its way goes dark.
patterns.thin: Thin liquidity: a large dark area near the price means few resting orders, the price can move through it quickly.

read.candles: Candles: supply actual OHLC bars on the same millisecond time and price axes. Missing periods remain empty; book snapshots are never used to invent executions. The last-price line uses the newest supplied trade or newer candle close.
read.navigation: History navigation: zooming and panning stop following. Select a retained time range in the navigator; reset restores the current market. getView / setView and viewChange share one viewport model.
read.intensity: Intensity filtering: intensityRange selects a 0–1 interval after color mapping. It does not change raw resting sizes, tooltip values or the automatic reference scale.
read.dataSemantics: This component displays resting liquidity and supplied execution candles. Examples use reproducible simulated matching. A liquidation heatmap requires its own liquidation data; resting order size is not liquidation size.

data.volumeAt: Hovered column: {{buys}} BTC bought, {{sells}} BTC sold
data.volumeHint: Hover a column to read its traded volume.
data.cellHint: Hover a cell to inspect it.
data.perpHint: Hover the heatmap to read the resting contracts and their value.
data.executionsOnly: Each 2-second candle aggregates actual executions from this seeded matching engine. Empty buckets are omitted; resting orders never become candles.
data.filterHint: Filter the normalized color intensity of resting liquidity. This changes visibility, not book sizes or executed volume.
data.navigatorHint: Move the range handles to inspect retained history. Follow the market restores the latest time and automatic price centering.
data.terminalHint: Seeded simulation, not an external exchange feed. All six metrics, execution candles and the ladder use the same matching engine. Summary metrics refresh once per second; book updates stream independently.
data.ladderAria: Current simulated BTC USDT order book

props.name: book
props.description: Book, applied when the object changes (stream updates through the ref)

props.name: trades
props.description: Trades; when the array grows, only the appended ones are added

props.name: bars
props.description: Candle history, passed through setBars when its identity changes

props.name: candles
props.description: Supplied OHLC bars drawn over liquidity; duration uses the lower median of the last 256 observed intervals (1 s for a single bar), leaving missing intervals empty.

props.name: lastPriceLine
props.description: Dashed latest trade price and axis tag; a bar opened after that trade supplies its newer close instead.

props.name: intensityRange
props.description: Inclusive normalized intensity range, after the color curve; display-only.

props.name: maxColumns
props.description: Maximum retained columns, clamped to 4–12000 and a 1000000 sampled-row budget.

props.name: maxBars
props.description: Maximum retained OHLC bars, clamped to 1–100000.

props.name: tickSize
props.description: Height of a price row (levels are aggregated into rows); a round multiple of the book's tick of about 0.1 basis point when omitted

props.name: interval
props.description: Time between two columns, in ms: the book is sampled at this pace

props.name: window
props.description: Visible time span, in ms (zoomable)

props.name: history
props.description: History kept, in ms (columns older than this are dropped)

props.name: depth
props.description: Price rows sampled on each side of the book per column

props.name: priceSpan
props.description: Visible price span (top − bottom); fits the best bid / ask of the window when omitted

props.name: colorScale
props.description: Scale from sizes to colors: `sqrt` keeps typical levels dim and lets significant liquidity glow, `linear` shows only the walls, `log` reveals thin liquidity next to them

props.name: sizeUnit
props.description: Unit of the sizes, shown after them in the legend and the tooltip (e.g. "BTC"); the numbers are not converted

props.name: legend
props.description: Legend of the color ramp (cold to hot, its size range) and of the trades, in the top-left corner of the plot

props.name: contrast
props.description: Multiplies the sizes before the scale: above 1 brightens thin liquidity (more of the field glows), below 1 keeps only the largest walls

props.name: maxSize
props.description: Size drawn with the hottest color (larger sizes saturate); when omitted, the 99th percentile of the visible non-empty cells (eased), so typical levels stay dark and only the top liquidity glows

props.name: colors
props.description: Color ramp, coldest first, interpolated in OKLab. The first color also fills the cells without liquidity (the field is opaque, no holes): make it a dark color in dark themes and a pale one in light themes. A perceptual heat ramp suited to the theme when omitted

props.name: bubbles
props.description: Trades drawn as bubbles sized by volume (buys / sells colors)

props.name: bubbleSize
props.description: Diameter of the largest bubble, in pixels (area ∝ volume, the smallest are 3 px dots)

props.name: bubbleVolume
props.description: Trade volume of the largest bubble; when omitted, the largest visible trade (eased)

props.name: bestLines
props.description: Best bid and ask lines

props.name: profile
props.description: Profile of the current book at the right edge

props.name: interactive
props.description: Wheel / pinch zoom and drag pan (double click resumes following the market)

props.name: tooltip
props.description: Hover crosshair and tooltip

props.name: renderer
props.description: Backend of the cells: the GPU when available

props.name: timeZone
props.description: Clock of the time axis and the tooltip: the local time or UTC (the clock of most exchanges)

props.name: labels
props.description: Overrides of the built-in texts, which follow `locale` (English, Chinese, Japanese and French built in)

props.name: upColor

props.name: downColor

props.name: colorConvention

examples.title: Backfill and live
examples.description: The book at the start of the history goes to setBook, then every recorded update with its exchange time (applyDeltas, addTrades): the heatmap samples it into one column per interval. The same calls then stream live. Drag to pan, Ctrl/⌘ + wheel zooms time, Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + wheel or dragging the price axis zooms prices, a double click follows the market again.

examples.title: Execution candles
examples.description: Actual simulated executions form sparse 2-second OHLC candles over the recorded resting liquidity.

examples.title: Color scale
examples.description: colorScale maps sizes to colors: sqrt keeps typical levels dim and lets significant liquidity glow, linear keeps only the walls, log reveals thin liquidity next to them. contrast multiplies the sizes first; maxSize fixes the hottest size (the 99th percentile of the visible data otherwise).

examples.title: Compact (mobile)
examples.description: A phone card: 30 seconds, profile={false} and smaller bubbles. Drag to pan, double tap to follow the market again.

examples.title: Dark terminal
examples.description: Colors come from the CSS variables of the container; colors sets the ramp (coldest first, after the floor color): the classic blue to red liquidity ramp on a terminal palette, with the time axis in UTC (timeZone) like most exchanges.

examples.title: History navigation
examples.description: Inspect retained history through the range navigator, then return to following the market.

examples.title: Intensity filter
examples.description: Use the range slider to isolate visible liquidity intensity without changing the underlying order book.

examples.title: Large trades
examples.description: The trades of a column are summed per side into one bubble, green for buys and red for sells (as the legend shows), whose area grows with the volume; bubbleVolume is the volume of the largest bubble (bubbleSize pixels). A lower contrast dims the book so the sweeps stand out; onHover reads the bought and sold volume of the hovered column.

examples.title: Heatmap, ladder and tape
examples.description: One recorded minute backfills the three widgets differently: the heatmap replays every update (applyDeltas, addTrades), the tape gets all its trades with setTrades, the ladder only the book of now. Each live message then goes to all three, like one exchange WebSocket.

examples.title: High-frequency stream
examples.description: A simulated fast market: about 100 book updates a second, one column every 50 ms, the last 15 seconds on screen. It reads like the charts above: bright lines are large orders, dots are trades, the bars on the right are the current book. Dragging or zooming stops following the market; Follow the market or a double click returns to now. The cells are drawn by the GPU (WebGPU or WebGL, Canvas2D otherwise): onRendererChange reports the backend, onFollowChange whether the view follows the market.

examples.title: Perpetual futures in contracts
examples.description: A BTC perpetual quoted in contracts of 0.001 BTC: formatSize converts the sizes, formatPrice shows dollars, sizeUnit and labels rename the units of the legend and tooltip, and timeZone="utc" matches the exchange clock of the funding countdown above.

examples.title: Price resolution and hover inspector
examples.description: tickSize sets the height of a price row (a new value resamples the replayed history), priceSpan fixes the visible price range instead of fitting the best bid and ask. With tooltip={false}, onHover drives a custom readout: column time, price row, resting size and side, traded volume.

examples.title: Red up, green down
examples.description: colorConvention="red-up": red buy bubbles and best bid line, green sells and best ask line.

examples.title: Liquidity terminal
examples.description: A complete simulated workspace: six market metrics, execution candles, liquidity filters, retained-history navigation and a synchronized order book.

examples.title: Time window, pause and clear
examples.description: window picks how much of the five recorded minutes (history) is on screen, without resampling. The switch stops the feed loop: the market resumes where it was, without a gap. clear() drops the columns, then setBook starts again from the current book.

data.volumeAt: Hovered column: {{buys}} BTC bought, {{sells}} BTC sold
data.volumeHint: Hover a column to read its traded volume.
data.cellHint: Hover a cell to inspect it.
data.perpHint: Hover the heatmap to read the resting contracts and their value.
data.executionsOnly: Each 2-second candle aggregates actual executions from this seeded matching engine. Empty buckets are omitted; resting orders never become candles.
data.filterHint: Filter the normalized color intensity of resting liquidity. This changes visibility, not book sizes or executed volume.
data.navigatorHint: Move the range handles to inspect retained history. Follow the market restores the latest time and automatic price centering.

OrderBookHeatmapProps.book: Book, applied when the object changes (stream updates through the ref)
OrderBookHeatmapProps.trades: Trades; when the array grows, only the appended ones are added
OrderBookHeatmapProps.onHover: Hovered cell (null when the pointer leaves)
OrderBookHeatmapProps.onRendererChange: Backend in use (also after a GPU loss)
OrderBookHeatmapProps.onFollowChange: true while the view follows the market, false after a zoom or pan
OrderBookHeatmapProps.ref: Imperative handle: setBook, applyDeltas, addTrades, resetView, getInstance
OrderBookHeatmapProps.bars: Supplied OHLC candles as object rows or typed columns; sent through setBars when the value changes. Candles are never inferred from the order book.
OrderBookHeatmapProps.onViewChange: Emits retained time bounds and the current time/price viewport, including follow mode.

OrderBookHeatmapHandle.setBook: Replaces the book (closes the columns up to its time)
OrderBookHeatmapHandle.applyDeltas: Applies updates (closes the columns up to their time)
OrderBookHeatmapHandle.clear: Removes the book, the history and the trades
OrderBookHeatmapHandle.setBars: Replace supplied OHLC candle history (object rows or typed columns).
OrderBookHeatmapHandle.updateBar: Update the latest supplied candle or append a newer candle.
OrderBookHeatmapHandle.setView: Set visible time and/or price bounds; pauses following the market.
OrderBookHeatmapHandle.getView: Read retained liquidity time bounds and the current viewport; null before mount.

OrderBookHeatmapOptions.tickSize: Height of a price row (levels are aggregated into rows); a round multiple of the book's tick of about 0.1 basis point when omitted
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.interval: Time between two columns, in ms: the book is sampled at this pace
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.history: History kept, in ms (older columns are dropped)
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.depth: Price rows sampled on each side of the book per column
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.priceSpan: Visible price span (top − bottom); fits the best bid and ask of the window when omitted
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.colorScale: Scale from sizes to colors: sqrt keeps typical levels dim and lets significant liquidity glow, linear shows only the walls, log reveals thin liquidity next to them
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.contrast: Multiplies the sizes before the scale: above 1 brightens thin liquidity (more of the field glows), below 1 keeps only the largest walls
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.maxSize: Size drawn with the hottest color (larger sizes saturate); when omitted, the 99th percentile of the visible non-empty cells (eased), so typical levels stay dark and only the top liquidity glows
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.sizeUnit: Unit of the sizes, shown after them in the legend and the tooltip (the numbers are not converted)
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.legend: Legend of the color ramp (cold to hot, its size range) and of the trades, in the top-left corner of the plot
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.colors: Color ramp, coldest first, interpolated in OKLab. The first color also fills the cells without liquidity (the field is opaque, no holes): a dark color in dark themes, a pale one in light themes. A perceptual heat ramp suited to the theme when omitted
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.bubbles: Trades drawn as bubbles sized by volume (buy and sell colors)
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.bubbleSize: Diameter of the largest bubble, in pixels (area ∝ volume, the smallest are 3 px dots)
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.bubbleVolume: Trade volume of the largest bubble; when omitted, the largest visible trade (eased)
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.profile: Profile of the current book at the right edge
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.interactive: Zoom and pan (a double click follows the market again)
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.renderer: Backend of the cells: the GPU when available
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.timeZone: Clock of the time axis and the tooltip: the local time or UTC (the clock of most exchanges)
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.labels: Overrides of the built-in texts, which follow locale (English, Chinese, Japanese and French built in)
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.candles: Draw supplied OHLC candles; enabled by default when bars are available.
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.lastPriceLine: Draw the latest supplied candle close as a price line.
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.intensityRange: Normalized lower and upper liquidity intensity bounds, each from 0 to 1.
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.maxColumns: Maximum retained liquidity columns; default 6000, bounded by the engine.
OrderBookHeatmapOptions.maxBars: Maximum retained supplied candles; default 20000, bounded by the engine.

OrderBookCommonOptions.upColor: Color of the bids and buys (the "up" side); --success-color by default, --danger-color with colorConvention "red-up"
OrderBookCommonOptions.downColor: Color of the asks and sells (the "down" side); --danger-color by default, --success-color with colorConvention "red-up"
OrderBookCommonOptions.colorConvention: "red-up" swaps the default colors: red bids and buys, green asks and sells (mainland China, Japan, Korea)
OrderBookCommonOptions.pricePrecision: Decimals of the prices; inferred from the data when omitted
OrderBookCommonOptions.sizePrecision: Decimals of the sizes; inferred from the data when omitted
OrderBookCommonOptions.locale: Locale of the numbers (Intl.NumberFormat, compact units such as k or 万) and of the built-in texts (English, Chinese, Japanese, French); the page language (lang attribute of the html element) when omitted
OrderBookCommonOptions.formatPrice: Formats a price (replaces pricePrecision and locale)
OrderBookCommonOptions.formatSize: Formats a size (replaces sizePrecision and locale)
OrderBookCommonOptions.fontFamily: Font of the texts; the theme font when omitted (a monospace font aligns the digits)
OrderBookCommonOptions.fontSize: Font size of the texts, in pixels
OrderBookCommonOptions.ariaLabel: Accessible name of the widget; the localized labels.name when omitted

OrderBookWidgetProps.height: Height of the widget; numbers are pixels
OrderBookWidgetProps.width: Width of the widget; numbers are pixels

OrderBookHeatmapLabels.liquidity: Resting size of the hovered cell
OrderBookHeatmapLabels.buys: Bought volume of the hovered column
OrderBookHeatmapLabels.sells: Sold volume of the hovered column
OrderBookHeatmapLabels.bid: Best bid, in the screen reader summary
OrderBookHeatmapLabels.ask: Best ask, in the screen reader summary
OrderBookHeatmapLabels.bidSide: Side badge of a hovered bid row in the tooltip
OrderBookHeatmapLabels.askSide: Side badge of a hovered ask row in the tooltip
OrderBookHeatmapLabels.bubbleHint: Legend row of the trades (bubble area = trade size)
OrderBookHeatmapLabels.name: Accessible name (when ariaLabel is not set)

OrderBookHeatmapHoverEvent.time: Start time of the hovered column
OrderBookHeatmapHoverEvent.price: Price of the hovered row; its lowest price when rows are aggregated into price buckets (rows thinner than 2 px)
OrderBookHeatmapHoverEvent.priceHigh: Highest price of the hovered row (equals price without aggregation)
OrderBookHeatmapHoverEvent.size: Resting size of the cell (summed over the bucket's prices)
OrderBookHeatmapHoverEvent.side: Side of the cell (null inside the spread)
OrderBookHeatmapHoverEvent.bar: Actual supplied OHLC candle covering the pointer time; absent in gaps.

MarketTrade.side: Aggressor side: "buy" lifted an ask, "sell" hit a bid

OrderBookHeatmapView.time: Visible start and end times, in epoch milliseconds.
OrderBookHeatmapView.follow: Whether the viewport follows the latest market.

OrderBookHeatmapViewInput.time: Visible start and end times, in epoch milliseconds.

OrderBookHeatmapViewData.availableTime: Earliest and latest retained liquidity times, or null when empty.
OrderBookHeatmapViewData.view: Current visible time/price bounds and follow state.

TradingBar.time: Opening time in milliseconds since the epoch

liquidity.title: Live liquidity heatmap
liquidity.description: A new book every 200 ms closes a column of resting size; trades are bubbles sized by volume.

red-up.title: Red-up colors, square-root scale
red-up.description: The mainland China convention (buys in red), a square-root color scale and no size profile.

candles-navigation.title: Supplied candles and history navigation
candles-navigation.description: Filter simulated liquidity and navigate history alongside 30 supplied OHLC candles aggregated from simulated executions.

props.options: Other engine options (OrderBookHeatmapOptions of minerva-design/charts/core: colors, texts, locale, labels…); property only
props.instance: The engine instance (minerva-design/charts/core), null until the element is rendered and connected
props.bars: Supplied OHLC candles as object rows or typed columns; sent through setBars when the value changes. Candles are never inferred from the order book.

events.minerva-hover: A cell is hovered; detail: { time, price, size, side, buyVolume, sellVolume }, null when the pointer left
events.minerva-renderer-change: The backend is ready, or fell back after a GPU loss; detail: { renderer }
events.minerva-follow-change: The view follows the market (true) or not after a zoom or a pan (false); detail: { follow }
events.minerva-view-change: Retained history or viewport changed; detail contains availableTime and view.

methods.resetView: Follows the market again (latest time, centered on the mid price)
methods.getRenderer: Backend in use (webgpu, webgl2, webgl, canvas2d), null until ready
methods.setBook: Replaces the book (closes the columns up to its time)
methods.applyDeltas: Applies updates (closes the columns up to their time)
methods.setBars: Replace supplied OHLC candle history (object rows or typed columns).
methods.updateBar: Update the latest supplied candle or append a newer candle.
methods.setView: Set visible time and/or price bounds; pauses following the market.
methods.getView: Read retained liquidity time bounds and the current viewport; null before mount.
methods.clear: Removes the book, the history and the trades
